A1.justification: Despite the title change, both PDFs describe the same FedALS and generalization-bound study. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and can be matched across the reorganization.

before.justification: Section 7, Figures 1-3, and Tables 1-3 report original federated-learning experiments with ResNet-20 and OPT-125M, including comparisons and sensitivity studies.

after.justification: Section 6 retains the original image-classification and MultiNLI experiments, comparative results, and sensitivity studies. These retained outcomes qualify as original empirical results.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1 and 4 replace mutually exclusive aggregation branches with separate conditions, allowing representation aggregation when head aggregation also occurs. Algorithm 1 also revises round indexing. These are limited corrections to the written procedure within the retained FedALS design, without evidence of experimental reruns.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate ResNet-20 on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, SVHN, and MNIST, and fine-tune OPT-125M on MultiNLI. The five-client iid and non-iid scenarios, including the layer-consensus example, are retained.

E2.justification: Figures 2-3 and Table 1 retain the same comparator membership: FedAvg versus FedALS in iid experiments, with SCAFFOLD and FedALS+SCAFFOLD also included in non-iid comparisons. Newly cited methods are not added to these evaluations.

E3.justification: Matched experiments retain their stated models, partitions, batch sizes, and aggregation settings. However, new Table 5 specifies Top-1 accuracy for LLM evaluation, while Figure 3 and Table 1 still report test loss. The PDFs do not resolve whether this is an intended protocol revision or a documentation error.

E4.justification: The layer-consensus case study, aggregation-frequency sensitivity study, and representation/head partition ablation retain the same questions and tested configurations. No new robustness test or supplementary analysis appears; Table 2's isolated uncertainty-value revision changes a result.

E5.justification: Both versions report 20 repetitions and means with standard deviations. New Tables 4-5 explicitly specify varying seeds and summarizing aggregated-model test performance over the last five rounds. This adds statistical reporting detail without establishing an increase in runs.

E6.justification: In Table 2, SVHN at alpha=25 changes from 0.7201 +/- 0.1565 to 0.7201 +/- 0.0549. Table 1's reduced decimal precision is equivalent rounding, and the remaining benchmark results, plotted findings, and Table 3 entries are retained.

T1.justification: Theorem 4.3, its appendix restatement, and Equation 58 remove the additive L/mu terms from both A and B, eliminating nonvanishing contributions to the R-round bound. This materially strengthens the stated guarantee. V3's formal convergence-rate Remark 5.1 is also removed; the one-round and partial-participation results remain.

C1.justification: Both versions claim improved federated-learning generalization bounds, a representation-motivated FedALS aggregation scheme, and communication/generalization benefits in non-iid settings. The new title and more cautious abstract wording do not materially redefine the contributions stated across the introduction and conclusion.

C2.justification: V3 motivates FedALS through relative model complexities and balancing component generalization, with excessive local steps limited by optimization error. V4's rewritten Section 5 instead develops a sample-size versus heterogeneity tradeoff, arguing that shared representations limit growth in non-iidness. The interpretation of performance degradation at large alpha changes accordingly.

D1.justification: V4 adds a code-access link and Appendix E.1-E.3 documenting Nesterov and Adam settings, learning-rate schedules, training budgets, and a more explicit tuning procedure. V3 supplied basic optimizers, batch sizes, and a broad grid-search description. These additions substantially expand reproducibility documentation without demonstrating changed experiments.

R1.justification: V4 expands positioning around pruning/quantization, layer-dependent representation theory, Sefidgaran et al. (2024), and Collins et al. (2022), while removing the complexity-measure literature and Koloskova-based discussion. The expanded comparisons distinguish statistical generalization from prior convergence and personalization results, substantially refocusing the literature-based rationale.

P1.justification: V4 retitles the paper, merges former Sections 5-6 into a rewritten FedALS section, expands the introduction and related work, and reorganizes experimental documentation into Appendix E.1-E.4. It also introduces substantially overlapping SCAFFOLD subsections 6.3 and 6.4. These are substantial narrative and structural revisions.

P2.justification: V4 changes the publication template, typography, and front matter, reflows existing figures, tables, and algorithms, and adds Tables 4-5 of experimental settings. Figures 1-3 retain their plotted content, and Tables 1-3 retain their comparison structures.

improvement.justification: V4 corrects aggregation control flow and adds useful reproducibility information. However, Table 5 contradicts the retained LLM loss results, and the central R-round bound drops L/mu terms while Equation 58 retains essentially the same citation-based justification. The supplied PDFs do not clarify whether this tightening is mathematically warranted, so its effect on reliability cannot be weighed confidently against the documentation gains.
